propositions: The Pass-2/Pass-3 judge exhibits self-consistency drift (unstable per-finding decisions) that injects noise into the Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary, threatening the reliability of new criteria like asserted_capability_confirmed added by R5.

Order permutation of plan sections flips gate verdicts with documented high frequency (82.5% of pairwise comparisons per Wang 2024), and residual order-sensitivity of the rubric-based gate must be empirically confirmed below a floor before R3 adds container criteria.

Experiment A measures self-consistency by re-judging 50 sampled findings (G6/E4/T3 cohort) 3 times each and computing Fleiss' κ and raw agreement; pass criterion is κ≥0.6 AND raw_agreement≥0.8, with any sub-floor result blocking R5.

Experiment B measures order-shuffle stability by judging 14 plans (≥3 top-level sections from corpus_sample.json) under 3 deterministically distinct section permutations each and computing agreement on verdict; pass criterion is κ≥0.6 AND raw_agreement≥0.8, with any sub-floor result failing R3 prerequisite.

Infra-INDETERMINATE verdicts (marked by coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed) are excluded and re-run as execution failures, not stable judge outcomes; genuine judge-INDETERMINATE (no flag set) is retained as a valid agreement category.

Exp A collects 3 votes per finding (150 agentic Pass-2 calls) using frozen committed inputs; Exp B collects 3 verdict judgments per plan (42 full-gate runs) by mutating a throwaway ticket-store clone while leaving the real store untouched.
